title: Replace a long serial prefix dependency with hierarchical local summaries

source.title: GPU Gems 3, Chapter 39: Parallel Prefix Sum (Scan) with CUDA
source.claim_scope: General associative scan decomposition demonstrated on historical NVIDIA hardware; current-device speedups, thresholds, and implementation details require target measurement.

implementation_recipe: Write the apparent serial recurrence as an explicit state transition and determine whether chunk summaries have an associative or otherwise composable combine rule.
Partition the long axis, compute independent local summaries and local prefixes, combine the chunk summaries, then finalize only the chunks or elements whose result depends on the global prefix.
Keep a direct serial path for small extents and compare one-stage, hierarchical, and library-primitive controls before tuning block geometry.
When only the first threshold crossing is needed, let partitions report bounded summary state and refine the winning partition instead of materializing every global prefix value.
validation_recipe: Test empty, singleton, non-power-of-two, duplicate-value, all-pass, none-pass, and boundary-crossing cases.
For floating-point scans, test values near the decision threshold and state whether reassociation is allowed by the numerical contract.
Measure each workload region separately because launch and summary overhead can dominate small batches or short rows.
Retain the serial implementation as a correctness oracle and as a guarded small-extent fallback.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: A serial dependency can shift to synchronization, summary communication, extra launches, or redundant local work.
At small extents, parallel decomposition can become launch-bound even when it reduces critical-path span.
failure_modes: The recurrence is not safely composable under the required ordering or floating-point semantics.
The implementation computes a full scan even though the output only needs a threshold location or compact summary.
Too many partitions make summary traffic and synchronization larger than the removed serial span.
Power-of-two assumptions or unstable tie handling break edge cases.
scope_limits: Associativity at the mathematical level does not automatically authorize floating-point reassociation.
The chapter's reported historical speedups are not evidence for a modern target GPU or a different operator.
A hierarchical scan is a candidate family, not a proof that scan is the dominant end-to-end bottleneck.

algorithmic_decomposition.baseline_dependency: A single lane or workgroup advances an ordered prefix state across the full logical extent.
algorithmic_decomposition.partition_axis: Split the longest ordered axis into contiguous chunks while preserving within-chunk order.
local_state: per-element local prefix or only the locally needed decision state
optional identity and validity flag for partial chunks
algorithmic_decomposition.combine_rule: Compose chunk summaries in order with an associative scan when legal, or use a bounded ordered summary pass when the number of chunks is small.
algorithmic_decomposition.finalization: Apply each chunk's incoming prefix to local results, or refine only the first chunk whose summary crosses the target condition.
algorithmic_decomposition.work_complexity: Prefer O(n) total work; reject naive O(n log n) global update schemes unless the frozen workload proves them faster.
algorithmic_decomposition.span_complexity: Reduce the long serial span from O(n) toward local-span plus summary-span, commonly O(n/p + log p) for p partitions.
algorithmic_decomposition.communication_cost: One summary write/read per partition plus any finalization traffic; include launch and synchronization costs in the bound.
invariants: chunk summaries compose to the same required result
tail elements and invalid lanes do not alter the summary
threshold ties follow the frozen contract
anti_patterns: tune warps around an unchanged single-lane recurrence
materialize a full prefix when only a boundary index is consumed
apply one configuration to both tiny and long extents

candidate_archetypes.name: local prefix plus chunk-summary scan
candidate_archetypes.template: Partition the ordered axis, compute local prefixes and one summary per partition, scan the summaries, then apply incoming state to each partition.

candidate_archetypes.name: summary then selective boundary refinement
candidate_archetypes.template: Have partitions report enough state to identify the first threshold-crossing partition, then refine only that partition while retaining a serial path for small extents.
